seoTitle: Free Bubble Level - Spirit Level with Phone Sensor
metaDescription: Use your phone's accelerometer as a spirit level with live X and Y tilt in degrees and a calibration button. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Lay your phone on a surface to see a bubble move and the tilt in degrees on two axes. A calibrate button sets the current position as zero.
why:
A spirit level is the quickest way to check that a shelf, a picture frame, a washing machine or a camera tripod is level, and it is rarely in your pocket when you need it. Your phone contains an accelerometer that can measure tilt, and this page turns it into a simple bubble level in the browser.

The tilt is calculated from gravity along the X and Y axes and shown in degrees, with a bubble that moves opposite to the tilt like a real vial. Because a phone case or the camera bump can leave the device slightly off flat, there is a calibrate button that sets the current angle as zero: place the phone on a surface you know is level, press it, then measure. Accuracy is good for casual jobs, not for precision engineering.
howTo: Open the page on a phone or tablet.
Press Enable level and allow motion access if asked.
Lay the device flat on the surface you want to check.
Read the X and Y degrees, and use Calibrate to set zero on a known level surface.

faq.a: Your device may have no accelerometer, which is common on desktop computers, or the page is not on HTTPS. On iPhones you must also allow motion access when prompted.
Roughly within a degree after calibration on most phones, which is fine for hanging a picture but not for building work. Cases, covers and the camera bump can add error, so calibrate each time.
Place the phone on a surface you trust to be level, such as a flat floor tile checked another way, and press Calibrate. Future readings are then shown relative to that position.
It is designed for flat surfaces with the phone lying down. Standing the phone on its edge changes which axes the readings represent, so results for walls will not be reliable.
